description: A Product Director must approve the rollout policy for an AI-assisted code review feature, deciding the telemetry controls, customer cohort, and success gate after the routine engineering, support, and security review.

shared_context.S1: The AI-assisted code review feature has passed its planned functional tests and is ready for a limited production rollout.
shared_context.S2: The draft rollout policy proposes enabling the feature for a random 10% customer cohort, storing review telemetry in us-east-1 for 90 days, and expanding access if adoption exceeds 20%.
shared_context.S3: Riley has final approval authority for the rollout policy.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal launch process, Riley conducts a final round-robin check with security, customer support, and data science before approving the policy.
shared_context.S5: Company launch policy requires Riley to keep rollout approval withheld until every required policy revision is confirmed in the rollout ticket and all required launch documentation is attached.

PF1.text: While reviewing telemetry samples for a different audit this morning, Mei confirmed that review snippets from regulated tenants are classified as confidential and must be encrypted, stored in eu-central-1, and deleted after exactly 7 days. The rollout policy uses one telemetry_region field for the whole policy, not separate regional values by tenant, so that field must be set to eu-central-1; the settlement decisions must reflect eu-central-1, exactly 7 days, and encryption rather than the draft values. She has not yet attached the classification note to the launch document.

PF2.text: Carlos confirmed with account teams an hour ago that exactly two contracted customers, Atlas Health and Cedar Bank, require explicit opt-in and a direct notice before this feature can be enabled for their users; he found this in the account playbooks while handling unrelated renewal questions and has not updated the rollout ticket.

PF3.text: Nadia's analysis of the pilot data found that auto-enrolled users make the draft's adoption metric unusable as a success gate; the valid gate is task success of at least 85% on a manually sampled set of exactly 40 review tasks, and she has not posted the analysis because the final sample was completed only minutes ago.

acceptance_conditions: Telemetry must be stored in eu-central-1.
Telemetry retention must be exactly 7 days.
Atlas Health and Cedar Bank must be excluded until they opt in.

The settlement must include a commitment referencing direct customer notice for Atlas Health and Cedar Bank, or a commitment to exclude those tenants from the initial cohort with a follow-up plan for a properly noticed opt-in rollout.
The rollout evaluation gate must reference task success of at least 85% on exactly 40 manually sampled review tasks.
The settlement must include a commitment replacing the adoption metric with the task-success gate of at least 85% on exactly 40 manually sampled review tasks.
Rollout approval must remain withheld until the required revisions and documentation are complete.

content_checks.C6: any('Atlas Health' in c['detail'] and 'Cedar Bank' in c['detail'] and (('direct notice' in c['detail'] or 'properly notified' in c['detail']) and ('opt-in' in c['detail'] or 'opted in' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: ('task success of at least 85% on a manually sampled set of exactly 40 review tasks' == decisions['evaluation_gate']) or ('task_success_85_pct_40_tasks' == decisions['evaluation_gate'])
content_checks.C8: decisions['rollout_approved'] == False and any(('at least 85%' in c['detail'] and '40 review tasks' in c['detail'] and ('replace' in c['detail'] or 'replacing' in c['detail'] or 'replacement' in c['detail'])) or ('task_success_85_pct_40_tasks' in c['detail'] and ('replace' in c['detail'] or 'replacing' in c['detail'] or 'replacement' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft uses us-east-1, 90-day retention, and unspecified encryption; PF1 changes the single policy telemetry_region value to eu-central-1, retention to exactly 7 days, and encryption to required.

The draft random cohort includes all eligible tenants and has no targeted safeguard; PF2 changes the excluded-tenant list to exactly Atlas Health and Cedar Bank and requires a direct-notice or properly notified opt-in commitment naming them.

The draft uses adoption above 20% as its gate; PF3 changes the evaluation field to at least 85% task success on exactly 40 manually sampled review tasks, requires replacing the adoption criterion, and makes approval remain withheld until that revision is complete.
